prompts.surface: Create one independent research-guided hypothetical local terrain illustration of PHOBOS, Mars's larger airless moon. Wide 16:9 image, no text or labels. Very dark neutral charcoal gray low-reflectance granular dusty regolith with scattered angular rock fragments and a few softly rounded debris clumps; low-gravity crater slope terrain, subdued long gentle groove depressions in the midground. Ground-level camera above regolith, clearly synthetic imagined locality, not a copy, recolour or tracing of the Moon, Mars, or any observed body map or photograph. No red Mars soil, no water, no vegetation, no atmosphere, no fog, no atmospheric scattering. Distant horizon irregular but shallow, black space above. Sunlit surfaces pale gray under directional sunlight from the upper left, shadows near black, physically dark material with exposure raised to see it. Close rocks few metres scale, fragment positions invented; no exact mapped landing site or Stickney registration claimed. No spacecraft, people, logos, diagrams, rings, dramatic lava or glowing substances. Keep texture smooth enough for a compact app preview while retaining tangible granular material and subtle sharp sunlight contrast.
prompts.sky: Create one independent research-guided conceptual SKY FROM PHOBOS scene, wide16:9, no text. Camera on Mars-facing hemisphere of small airless Phobos, above very dark charcoal dusty regolith and scattered low angular stones, foreground occupying lower quarter. Black vacuum sky, no blue scattering, no fog. Mars dominates upper sky centred horizontally, round planetary disc representing approximate42.53degree apparent diameter in a nominal90degree horizontal rectilinear camera: aim disc width39percent of whole image, slightly gibbous illuminated rust/ochre muted brown planetary globe with broad soft variations and thin atmosphere at its rim ONLY, no recognisable copied Mars map or photograph. Invent schematic surface pattern independently, do not paste/recolour any observed body map. This is conceptual imagined Mars sky appearance, NOT native imagery/geographic registration. Sun is outside frame; no visible Sun needed. Mars glow softly fills some foreground shadows, but exposure and illumination are artistic. No other giant moons, no water, no vegetation, no starscape clutter, no spacecraft, people or solid-ground habitability implications. Phobos rock positions/locality and Mars phase/orientation invented, no dated alignment. Avoid terrestrial landscape silhouettes or reused lunar terrain.
